unexplained_peaks — DRIVE pxrd op

• Data kinds: table → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.unexplained_peaks(fit_result, intensity=None, min_snr=6.0, index=True, noise=None, known_ratio=0.25, model_error=0.1) (to call the implementation directly, import pxrd; pxrd.unexplained_peaks(fit_result, intensity=None, min_snr=6.0, index=True, noise=None, known_ratio=0.25, model_error=0.1); from the registry, opsdrive.get("unexplained_peaks"))

Usage

Extracts, from the residual of the phase-fraction fit, the peaks that no phase in the dictionary can explain (clues to an unknown phase).

Applies diffraction_peaks to the residual (fit_result of residual, or intensity − fit) and keeps only positive peaks. A residual peak sitting on a strong line of a known phase (height less than known_ratio times the known-phase model at that position) is likely a remnant of width or shape mismatch, so it is marked near_known=True and excluded from indexing (returned, not deleted). If 3 or more

remain, cubic_index attempts cubic indexing (index=True, up to 1/3 outliers allowed). If the lattice of a known phase is off, the residual shows "positive-negative pairs" that become false peaks — in that case use lattice_tolerance of phase_fractions first. The proper thing is to pass the noise of azimuthal_integrate as sigma (if absent, it is estimated from the residual's MAD). The noise used to judge peaks is sqrt(noise² + (model_error × 既知相の模型)²) — with high counts the Poisson σ is small, and slight shape mismatch of a strong known line (remnant of approximating the box-shaped pixel spread with a Gaussian; rwp 2 to 4 % on synthetic images) looks like a "peak" of thousands of σ, so the relative error of the model itself is put into the noise floor.

Returns (dict): two_theta / d [Å] / height / fwhm / snr / near_known (bool) / index (result of cubic_index or None).

Raises ValueError: fit_result not in the form of phase_fractions, length mismatch.
